maritime.title: NERAI Maritime Weekly
events: Saudi East-West Pipeline struck and shut, last Hormuz bypass eliminated
Hormuz forward risk falls 6.8 pts to 44% even as physical flow hits -96.4% — a critical divergence
Houthis seize Mocha port and Perim Island, placing Bab el-Mandeb under direct control
Iranian commercial vessel struck near Qeshm/Hormuz, 1 killed — fresh attack in active conflict zone
Eastern Mediterranean 8-week risk hits 82% — highest forward probability in NERAI corpus
maritime.summary: The Gulf crisis deepened across multiple fronts this week: Hormuz physical oil flow collapsed to 0.7 mb/d (-96.4% vs baseline, SEVERE), the Saudi East-West Pipeline was struck and shut down — eliminating the primary Hormuz bypass — while Houthi forces seized Perim Island and the port of Mocha, tightening their grip on Bab el-Mandeb. Against this, the NERAI 4-week disruption probability for Hormuz fell 6.8 points to 44%, a divergence from the physical collapse that is itself the key analytic signal of the week. Diplomatic back-channels flickered: an Oman-mediated Hormuz routing agreement was reported but an Iranian official cautioned no signed deal was yet expected from Monday's meeting.

sanctions.title: NERAI Sanctions Weekly
events: US Sanctions All 27 Remaining Active Iranian Airlines in 36-Target Aviation Sweep
US Sanctions Networks Aiding Iran Proxies Across Middle East in Expanded Campaign
UN Security Council Rolls Over Sudan Darfur Embargo One Month; Nationwide Ban Unresolved
OFAC Sanctions Chinese Cybercrime Platform Xinbi Guarantee; $24B Alleged Fraud Ring Dismantled
Switzerland Bans Purchase and Import of Sudanese Gold, Squeezing War Economy
sanctions.summary: The week was dominated by a sweeping US aviation sanctions package against Iran — the largest single-sector designation in recent memory — complemented by a parallel action targeting Iran's proxy-financing networks across the Middle East and a cybercrime/sanctions-evasion sweep against a Chinese-run platform. The UN Security Council took a minimalist path on Sudan, rolling over the Darfur-only embargo for one month while US pressure for a nationwide ban remains unresolved. Switzerland's new Sudanese gold import ban added a meaningful multilateral flanking measure to an otherwise stalled Sudan enforcement picture.
